blocks.text: 5 January: Argentine Side of Iguazu Falls – Buenos Aires

provenance.wordAbsenceReason: The approved Word 2027 has a Day 7 dated heading and transfer narrative, but not this exact combined standalone itinerary title.

blocks.text:
After breakfast, set out with an English-speaking guide to explore the Argentine side of Iguazu Falls. The journey crosses the Iguazu River via the Tancredo Neves Bridge.

Yesterday you saw the falls from a distance; today, the walkways take you much closer. Some paths cross above the river while others descend towards the lower cascades. At times the water is beneath your feet; at others, it seems almost level with your eyes.

The Argentine side involves more walking along the pathways, but this is where you can truly feel the river's power. At some viewpoints the water rushes past almost within reach; from others you look down onto individual cascades. The two days at Iguazu are therefore very different: the first provides an overview, while the second brings you close to the details and the force of the water.

The highlight of the route is the Devil's Throat. First you hear the roar and see a white cloud rise above the gorge. From the edge, you can watch the river plunge down in a broad torrent just beside the walkway.

After the excursion, transfer to the airport for your flight to Buenos Aires. On arrival, your driver will meet you at the airport and take you to your hotel.
